name: Senegal
headline: Senegal: +6.7% growth in 2025, 1.4% inflation, debt 128% of GDP
sections: Senegal is a $37.1 billion economy (2025), the world's 110th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +6.7% in 2025, faster than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $5,463 at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 13.2% of GDP (2025).
Consumer prices rose 1.4% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 9.7% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 2.7% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 3.6% (2025).
Gross government debt is 128% of GDP (2025), a very high level that has risen from 91% in 2020. The general government balance is −6.4% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is −1.2% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 71% of GDP (2025), a fairly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 0.1% of GDP (2025).
Life expectancy is 68.9 years (2024). Population: 19.2 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
